rationale: C22 is a direct and highly material template. Both proclamations invoke section 22 of the Agricultural Adjustment Act, recount the same September 5, 1939 cotton-quota proclamation and its modifications, describe a supplemental Tariff Commission investigation with notice, a public hearing, findings, recommendations, a transcript, and transmission to the Secretary of Agriculture, and then modify the same proclamation for long-staple cotton using nearly identical operative language. C14 has some analogous transitional-quota language, while C07 uses similar amendment-by-reference machinery, but neither approaches C22's specificity.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the United States Tariff Commission has made a supplemental investigation to determine whether the circumstances requiring the said import quota on cotton having a staple of 1 1/8 inches or more in length continue to exist, or whether changed circumstances require the modification of the quota or of the methods of administering it
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the United States Tariff Commission has made a supplemental investigation to determine whether the circumstances requiring the import quotas on cotton having a staple of 1 1/8 inches or more in length continue to exist, or whether changed circumstances require the modification of the quotas for the quota year beginning September 20, 1947 or for subsequent quota years
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive near-verbatim description of the same agency investigation into the continuing need for the same long-staple-cotton quota.

shared_material.child_excerpt: after due notice, a public hearing was held on July 7, 1949, at which parties interested were given opportunity to be present, to produce evidence, and to be heard, and, in addition to the hearing, the Commission made such investigation as it deemed necessary for a full disclosure and presentation of the facts
shared_material.parent_excerpt: after due notice, a public hearing was held on February 17, 1948, at which parties interested were given opportunity to be present, to produce evidence, and to be heard, and, in addition to the hearing, the Commission made such investigation as it deemed necessary for a full disclosure and presentation of the facts
shared_material.explanation: The later proclamation reuses an unusually detailed recital almost word for word, changing principally the hearing date.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Commission has made findings of fact and has transmitted to me a report of such findings and its recommendations based thereon, together with a transcript of the evidence submitted at the hearing, and has also transmitted a copy of such report to the Secretary of Agriculture
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the Commission has made findings of fact and has transmitted to me reports of such findings and its recommendations based thereon, together with a transcript of the evidence submitted at the hearing, and has also transmitted a copy of such reports to the Secretary of Agriculture
shared_material.explanation: Near-identical account of the administrative record and interagency transmission.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do hereby find and proclaim, on the basis of the investigation and report of the United States Tariff Commission, that changed circumstances require the further modification ... of the said proclamation of September 5, 1939 ... Accordingly ... I hereby further modify the said proclamation
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do hereby find and declare, on the basis of the investigation and reports of the United States Tariff Commission, that changed circumstances require the modification of the said proclamation of September 5, 1939 ... Accordingly ... I hereby modify the said proclamation
shared_material.explanation: The operative finding-and-modification sequence is substantially the same legal machinery applied to a new quota-year adjustment.
